text:
Alex: Heads-up — release window at 16:00 UTC. Quick question before we lock: for hotfixes should we pin deploys to a commit hash or just bump the semver patch and tag?
Maria (PM): For customers I prefer a patch bump so changelog + release notes are clear. End users see v1.4.3 not a git sha.
Jamal (SRE): Pinning to hash is operationally safer for rollbacks. Our rollback playbook expects exact commit ids. Deploy-bot currently accepts either `tag:` or `commit:`.
Nina (Eng): Agree with Jamal on rollbacks, but patch-only approach means we sometimes have multiple commits under the same patch if we backport, which makes diffing release history annoying.
Alex: Right — tradeoff is clarity vs traceability. We also have CI that can auto-create annotated tags.
deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: `/deploy prod v1.4.2` by @Alex — will run canary for 5m then promote.
Maria (PM): If we do patch bumps, can we include commit short in the release notes? e.g. "v1.4.3 — fix leak (commit abcd123)"
Nina (Eng): We could use semver build metadata: `v1.4.3+abcd123`. Semver allows it but some tooling (npm, pip) ignores build metadata for ordering. Also tags with `+` can be weird in shells.
Jamal (SRE): Another option: keep `v1.4.3` as the public tag, and create an auxiliary tag `prod-2026-03-10-abcd123` for operational pinning. Deploys reference the aux tag.
CI Bot: Suggestion: CI can create 2 refs on release: annotated `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` + `deploy/MINOR/PATCH/sha` (e.g., `deploy/1.4/3/abcd123`). We already push `refs/tags/` and `refs/heads/` in CI.
Alex: That sounds reasonable — single canonical semver for external + a machine tag for infra. Less user-visible semver clutter.
Maria (PM): Works for me. For release notes: include one-line summary + full commit diff link + short commit sha. Keep in the changelog entry.
Nina (Eng): Small nit: we should document the exact naming rules. Proposal: annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` (signed), auxiliary tag `deploy/X.Y.Z/SHORTSHA`, and the deploy-bot will prefer auxiliary tags for rollbacks.
Jamal (SRE): And add a CI job that verifies when a `vX.Y.Z` tag exists it references the same commit as `deploy/X.Y.Z/SHORTSHA` (fail fast if mismatch).
Alex: OK let's make this the new default for hotfixes & patches. Action items: 1) Nina — add short doc with naming conventions and a couple examples in the release playbook; 2) CI team — add verification job; 3) Ops — update rollback playbook to use auxiliary tag.
Maria (PM): I'll update the release notes template to include the commit link and the auxiliary tag name.
Nina (Eng): I'll open a tiny PR to docs and add a snippet you can copy into the playbook.
Jamal (SRE): I'll queue a follow-up to update the rollback runbook after CI job merges.
Alex: Nice. Triage: keep this policy for today's window. If anyone sees an edge-case (binary releases, external package managers), flag it asap.
Maria (PM): :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Note: if you try `/deploy prod commit abcd123` and no aux tag exists, deploy-bot will create a temporary deploy-ref `deploy/tmp/abcd123` for the run and annotate the release message.
CI Bot: Example commands in CI: ```
# create annotated semver tag
git tag -a v1.4.3 -m "release v1.4.3"
# create auxiliary deploy tag
git tag deploy/1.4.3/abcd123 abcd123
git push origin refs/tags/v1.4.3 refs/tags/deploy/1.4.3/abcd123
```
Alex: Perfect. Thanks all — will proceed with hybrid policy for patch hotfixes today.
